title: alyssum calycinum var. sublineare
intro: Alyssum calycinum var. sublineare, commonly known as Creeping Rosemary, is a low-growing, spreading perennial plant native to Europe and Asia. It is valued for its tiny blue flowers and fragrance. The plant has been used in traditional medicine to treat various health issues, including digestive problems, stress, and anxiety, due to its health benefits such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions include its sedative and calming effects, which are attributed to the bioactive constituents such as essential oils, flavonoids, and phenolic acids present in the plant.
